passage:
"Two minutes to the call," Santosh said. "You look like you're bracing for the dentist."
"I'm tired. The server mess last night." Lalit rolled his shoulders. "But Mr. Rao's team is nervous about the new timeline, so I want to start warm."
"Fake smile?"
"Not fake. I do like these people. I'm just choosing to show that part first." He unclenched his jaw. "Slower voice, and I'll actually look at the camera."
"And the tiredness?"
"Tell you after, over chai."
Twenty-five minutes later Lalit closed the laptop and slumped.
"How was it?" Santosh asked.
"They relaxed by the third minute. Now I need ten minutes with no face on at all."
"Take them. I'll bring the chai."

qa.q: Which team is nervous about the new timeline?
qa.a: Mr. Rao's team is nervous about the new timeline.

qa.q: What does Lalit want from his warm start, and how does he feel underneath?
qa.a: He wants the nervous team to settle, while he is tired from the server mess last night. He says he likes these people, so the warmth looks like a choice rather than a cover, though he may also be a little anxious about the timeline.

qa.q: What keeps Lalit's deliberate warmth from turning into constant suppression?
qa.a: He is honest with Santosh about being tired, saves his real state for after the call, and takes ten minutes with no face on. That way the display is a skill for the meeting, not all-day hiding. 🙂

qa.q: How might Mr. Rao's team feel in the first minutes of the call?
qa.a: They probably feel reassured by the slower voice and steady eye contact. They don't know Lalit is tired, and a tense face might have made them more worried about the timeline.

grounding: Illustrates choosing a warm expression on purpose for a client call as a normal social skill, without suppressing real feelings afterwards.

passage:
I used to think choosing my expression was a kind of lying. Then, one Tuesday before a client review, I caught myself relaxing my forehead and lifting my voice on purpose, and it felt like putting on a good shirt, not a mask. It worked; the client's frown eased. The trouble came the next month, when a project went wrong and I kept the same calm face for three days, even with my own team. Sumit stopped by my desk and said, "You've been very composed lately. Is it real, or is it the client face?" I laughed, then admitted it was the client face. We had a proper talk. Now I choose the composed look for the call and let it go afterwards.
— Mridul

qa.q: How many days did Mridul keep the same calm face after the project went wrong?
qa.a: Mridul kept the same calm face for three days.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling on laughing at Sumit's question?
qa.a: Probably caught out and a little relieved, since Mridul then admitted it was the client face. The laugh could also have been a nervous way of dodging the question for a moment.

qa.q: What could Mridul do after a tense client call so the composed face doesn't follow Mridul through the week?
qa.a: Mridul can let the composed look go once the call ends and talk honestly with someone like Sumit about the real feelings underneath. 😊

qa.q: How might Sumit have seen Mridul's three days of calm?
qa.a: Sumit may have found it too steady to be entirely natural and wondered if something was being held in. Sumit asked rather than assuming, which left Mridul room to answer.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional choosing a composed display on purpose and noticing when it slides into constant suppression.

passage:
Mentoring notes, Thursday. Written by Madhav, team lead.

Sat in on Jasleen's renewal call with the logistics client. The client opened by criticising our last report for five minutes. Jasleen kept a steady, warm voice, nodded on camera, smiled when she thanked them for the detail, then walked them through the fix. It was a good call; the client ended by booking the next review.

After we disconnected she rubbed her cheeks and said, "My face hurts from being pleasant." She laughed, but it was the fourth call like this this week.

What I did: asked how she was actually doing. She admitted she'd been swallowing irritation all week and going home flat. We agreed she'll take ten minutes between difficult calls, and that "let me check and come back to you" is always allowed. I'll check in with her again on Monday.

qa.q: How many calls like this had Jasleen had this week?
qa.a: It was the fourth call like this this week.

qa.q: What does Jasleen rubbing her cheeks and saying her face hurts suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: It suggests she was tired and had been holding back irritation behind a pleasant face; it could also simply be relief that a hard call went well.

qa.q: How could Madhav keep supporting Jasleen after this call?
qa.a: Madhav could keep the Monday check-in, protect the ten-minute breaks, and remind her that saying she needs to check and come back is fine.

qa.q: How might the client have experienced Jasleen's warm, steady manner?
qa.a: The client probably felt heard rather than argued with, which may be why they booked the next review.

grounding: It shows a young professional choosing a warm, composed face on a client call and a lead noticing when it starts to become constant suppression.

passage:
Wednesday, late.

Big pitch today. Vidya said on the way in, "Whatever happens, keep your face calm. They watch us more than the slides."

Then slide twelve was the old version, with last year's figures. My stomach dropped. I could feel heat climbing my neck. But I'd decided in the lift that I'd stay composed on purpose, so I kept my hands open on the table, slowed my voice and said, "Let me give you the current figure instead," and just said it from memory.

Vidya caught my eye and gave the smallest nod.

It worked. They asked good questions, not about the mistake.

On the bus home I let it all out in a long voice note to Pema about how rattled I was. I think that's the deal: I can wear calm for an hour, as long as I take it off afterwards somewhere safe.

Tenzin

qa.q: Which slide showed the old version with last year's figures?
qa.a: Slide twelve was the old version with last year's figures.

qa.q: What was Tenzin feeling when slide twelve came up, and how do we know?
qa.a: Tenzin felt panic and embarrassment, shown by the stomach dropping and heat climbing the neck, though the calm face was a deliberate choice to cover it.

qa.q: What did Tenzin's approach do well?
qa.a: Tenzin chose a composed display for the meeting and then let the rattled feeling out later in a voice note, so the calm did not become constant bottling.

qa.q: What would change if Tenzin never took the calm off afterwards?
qa.a: The stress would pile up with nowhere to go, and the useful skill could turn into hiding feelings all the time.

grounding: It illustrates a young professional deliberately choosing a composed expression in a pitch and releasing the real feeling later.

passage: Binita's phone buzzed with her brother's angry voice note about the quarrel over the family field boundary, just as the call from the buyer in Pune came through. Her jaw was tight. In the tin-roofed cooperative office near Sangli, with hens scratching outside the door, she rolled her shoulders, put on the warm voice she kept for buyers and smiled so it would reach her words. "Namaskar, Mehra-ji! Yes, the ghee shipment leaves Friday. We're very glad to have your order again." The buyer laughed and added twenty tins. When the call ended, Binita let the smile drop. Abhinav, who kept the accounts at the next desk, looked up. "You sounded happy." "I chose to sound happy," she said. "I'm actually furious with my brother." She stepped out, walked to the well and back, and then called her brother to talk it through in her ordinary voice.

qa.q: What shipment did Binita say would leave on Friday?
qa.a: The ghee shipment would leave Friday.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling while she spoke warmly to the buyer?
qa.a: Binita was furious with her brother after the voice note but chose a warm voice on purpose; the tight jaw showed the anger was still there under the smile.

qa.q: Which part of Binita's handling was healthy, and why?
qa.a: The warm voice for the buyer was an ordinary work skill, and she also named the anger to Abhinav and took a walk, so the feeling was not simply buried.

qa.q: How might Abhinav read Binita's cheerful calls if she never explained?
qa.a: Abhinav might believe she was always genuinely happy and miss the times she needed a moment, which could lead him to misjudge her mood.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional choosing a warm display for a client call on purpose while still acknowledging the real feeling afterwards.
